name: Bai-Perron Last-Segment Allocator
note: Bai-Perron multiple mean shifts, fitted by dynamic programming to the trailing return series with a minimum segment length and at most m breaks, the number of breaks chosen by BIC or LWZ. Everything before the LAST estimated break is thrown away and the annualised Sharpe of only the post-break segment sets the weight w = clip(|SR|/sr_norm, 0, 1); a rolling window blends across breaks by construction, and this one refuses to. The harness cannot vary position size, so w acts as a GATE (trade only while w >= w_min) rather than a multiplier, and the base strategy being allocated to is the symbol itself -- long while the current regime's Sharpe is positive, short while it is negative. The daily half of the rule is kept: a fresh break inside the last `fresh` bars whose post-break mean is negative flattens and blocks new entries until the next rebalance. Break dates are searched on a grid of bstep bars to keep the DP affordable per bar.
source: Bai, J. & Perron, P. (1998) Econometrica 66:47-78 and (2003) Journal of Applied Econometrics 18:1-22, sequential sup-F(l+1|l) testing for multiple unknown breaks; empirical motivation from Alexander, N. & Fabozzi, F.J., 'Measuring Strategy-Decay Risk: Minimum Regime Performance and the Durability of Systematic Investing', arXiv:2604.08356, Exhibit 3 (per-factor split dates and left/right Sharpe ratios).
